A1.justification: Both complete 27-page PDFs describe the same work, Gumbel Counterfactual Generation from Language Models. The main text, figures, algorithm, equations, and Appendices A–E are readable and support direct comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original counterfactual-generation experiments, including edit-distance distributions, targeted knowledge-editing outcomes, and generated examples in Section 4 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and their quantitative and qualitative outcomes in Section 4 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: The Gumbel-max WSEM construction, hindsight noise sampling, and counterfactual generation procedure remain unchanged, including Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: Both versions use English Wikipedia prompts, Bios professor biographies, and intervention-focused Louvre and koala scenarios. Appendix D settings and Appendix E examples introduce no different coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 2 retains the same six evaluated intervention variants: gender steering on both models, LLaMA3 honesty steering and instruction tuning, and GPT2-XL MEMIT-Louvre and MEMIT-Koalas. No comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: Both retain 500 Wikipedia-prompted generations per model pair, five-word prompts, multinomial sampling, a 25-token continuation limit, and normalized edit distance. The targeted Louvre evaluation retains nucleus sampling and 75 filtered sentences.

E4.justification: The intervention side-effect analysis, targeted editing case studies, and Wikipedia and gender examples in Appendix E are unchanged. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Figure 2 retains the same sentence-level distributions and median markers. Neither version reports additional repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figure 2's plotted data and the examples in Figures 3–5 and Appendix E are unchanged. Both report MEMIT edit distances of 10–15% and Louvre counterfactuals mentioning Rome in 54.6% of cases and Paris in 45.4%.

T1.justification: Definition B.1, Eq. (8), replaces equality of random variables with equality in distribution, a localized correction to the formal definition. The WSEM construction, theorem statements, and proofs otherwise remain unchanged; Proposition 3.1's proof reference is merely relocated.

C1.justification: The claims about generating counterfactual strings through inferred Gumbel noise and exposing intervention side effects are retained. Replacing 'generalized' with 'well-founded' SEMs in the conclusion aligns terminology with the existing construction.

C2.justification: The substantive interpretations of autoregressive semantic drift, intervention side effects versus spurious associations, and dependence on the chosen causal mechanism remain unchanged. The limitations and alternative-mechanism discussion in Appendix B are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix D retains the same hyperparameters, intervention layers, 15,000 biography pairs, model-access links, and eight RTX-4096 GPUs using 32-bit precision. No implementation or reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning, including Appendix A's comparison with concurrent work, are unchanged. The replacement URL for Gumbel (1954) is a bibliographic update to the same work.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized grammar and wording edits, clarifies WSEM terminology, and relocates a proof cross-reference. It also updates affiliations and publication headers and adds acknowledgements, while retaining the section structure.

P2.justification: All five figures retain their content and display design. Reduced whitespace and text reflow alter the surrounding layout, bringing the results opening onto page 8 and the complete conclusion onto page 10; bibliography wrapping also changes.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves precision and readability through the explicit distributional equality in Definition B.1, consistent WSEM terminology, and localized grammatical corrections. The scientific scope, experimental evidence, and limitations remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
